description: Side leg raise guide: lift the straight top leg to train the side glutes that keep your pelvis level. Covers mistakes plus easier and harder versions.
intro: The side leg raise is a simple side-lying lift of a straight leg. It strengthens the side glutes and hip muscles that keep your pelvis level on every step. For runners and cyclists it supports the pelvis from the outside; it is not a direct pelvic floor exercise.
feel: You should feel effort on the outside of your top hip and the side of your buttock. You should not feel it mostly in the front of the thigh, the lower back or the waist. Place a hand on the side of the hip: it should firm as the leg rises. If your toes turn up toward the ceiling, the front of the thigh has taken over.

mistakes.right: Raise it only a short way. Past that, the waist and back take over.
Keep your hips stacked and the leg in line with your body or slightly behind it, never in front.

mistakes.wrong: Swinging the leg up and letting it drop
mistakes.right: Lift over two seconds, lower over two to three, and do not rest the leg between reps.

easier: Bend the bottom knee for a steadier base, lift less, or do the raise standing while holding a chair.
harder: Hold the top for three seconds, add a light ankle weight or a band around the ankles, or move slower.
who: Good for runners, cyclists, people with weak hips, and women who want stronger support around the pelvis.
skip: Check with a doctor or physiotherapist first if lying on your side hurts the hip or back, after recent hip or pelvic surgery, or with pelvic girdle pain in pregnancy. A pillow under your head and between your knees can help. Stop if it hurts.

faq.q: What muscles does a side leg raise work?
faq.a: Mainly the gluteus medius and minimus on the side of the hip, plus deep hip muscles that help keep the pelvis level.

faq.q: Are side leg raises good for runners?
faq.a: Yes. They are a common part of hip strength work for runners because these muscles control the pelvis on each stride.
